absent: Full memory layout of audit entry, rule, field, context, names, tree reference, watch, parent and mark structures beyond members referenced in these fragments.
Hash function and bucket count used for inode based rule lookup and collision handling.
Exact semantics of numeric, identifier and permission comparators and operator encodings beyond delegation described here.
Security module rule initialization and matching internals, property formats and error codes beyond temporary invalid handling.
Filesystem notification mark allocation, update and release lifecycle beyond the event paths shown.
Priority assignment policy, ordering guarantees and persistence of priority bounds beyond initial values and comparison gate.
User control plane for installing, replacing and removing rules and reporting events beyond in kernel filtering.
Lock ordering with other subsystems and blocking constraints beyond read side and mutex use shown.
Allocation contexts and failure handling for initial entry creation beyond error pointer return.

findings.text: Rule duplication creates a fresh entry sized by the source field count and copies scalar control state covering flags, persistence flags, list selector, action, mask words, priority, buffer length, inode selector and field count. The directory tree handle is shared without added referencing. Field storage is copied elementwise before selected kinds receive deep handling, and an existing watch reference is transferred at completion.

During duplication, subject and object identity fields are refreshed through a dedicated LSM helper, filter key text is duplicated as a new string, and executable identity is duplicated through a helper that receives caller context. Any failure detaches a partially installed executable mark, releases the new entry, and reports an error pointer, with memory exhaustion distinguished from helper failure codes.

Executable duplication duplicates the pathname text from the old mark and then allocates a new filesystem notification mark bound to the new rule using the supplied context and pathname length. Pathname memory is released when mark allocation fails. Memory exhaustion and mark allocation failure are reported with distinct error encodings.

LSM field duplication makes a private copy of the source LSM text and then reinitializes the destination LSM rule object for its type, operator and text. A policy validation failure that indicates temporary invalidity is retained with a warning and treated as success so the rule can become valid after a later policy reload.

Inode based filtering has no effect for audit daemon tasks. For other tasks it holds RCU read side protection while walking the context names list in order, delegating each name to per inode filtering, stopping at the first match, and then releasing protection.

Per inode filtering hashes the supplied name inode number to select a hash bucket and then applies generic operation filtering with the calling task, the syscall context, the selected bucket, the name and the major operation identifier.

Generic operation filtering walks a rule list with RCU list iteration, testing each entry for mask membership of the operation before evaluating the full rule predicate. On the first entry satisfying both tests, the resulting state is stored in the context and success is reported. Exhaustion without a match reports no match.

Rule evaluation first discards rules whose priority does not exceed the stored context priority. Remaining rules require every field to match. A single non matching field rejects the rule. On full match with a context present, the context filter key is replaced by a fresh duplicate of the rule filter key when present and the context priority is advanced to the rule priority.

A fully matching rule translates its configured action into context state, with the never action selecting the disabled state and the always action selecting the record state, and reports a match. Rules that do not fully match leave the output state untouched and report no match.

Process identity matching derives the thread group identifier for process checks, lazily caches the parent identifier in the context for parent checks, and compares personality, session identifier, login identifier and login set flag using equality style comparison against the stored field value.

Architecture, exit code, success indication, argument values and socket family depend on syscall context presence. Exit and success additionally require a valid return encoding, with success interpreting the expected value as a choice between success and failure markers. Argument selection indexes the context argument vector by distance from the first argument selector. Socket family requires a stored socket address.

User and group matching uses dedicated comparators for real, effective, saved and filesystem variants. Primary and effective group equality additionally consults supplementary membership when direct comparison fails, while inequality conditionally negates the membership outcome. Object user and group selectors match either the supplied name or any entry in the context names list.

Device major, device minor, inode number and object ownership selectors match either the supplied name or, when no name is supplied, any entry in the context names list. Device checks consider both the device and the raw device of each candidate. Watch comparison uses the stored watch against supplied name location with optional negation. Directory matching tests context tree references for membership with optional negation.

Subject identity matching obtains current subject properties once per rule evaluation and reuses the result across subject fields. Fields lacking an initialized LSM rule object do not match. Object identity matching checks the supplied name, then each names list entry, then the interprocess object when the context denotes interprocess communication.

The filter key selector always succeeds and is ignored for filtering decisions. Permission and file type selectors delegate to dedicated helpers with optional negation of the helper outcome. The generic cross field selector delegates to a dedicated identity comparison routine.

Permission matching classifies the syscall by architecture and number and then applies class specific logic. Native and compat paths test requested read, write and attribute bits against class membership. Open paths intersect the requested mask with access mode derived from the relevant argument or extended flags. Socket path matches bind with write request, exec path tests exec request, and unknown classes yield no match.

Syscall class matching validates the syscall number against bitmask capacity and the class index against configured range and presence before testing the corresponding bit. Registration allocates a zeroed bitmask, populates bits from a terminated list with range validation, rejects duplicate or out of range class installation, and installs the new mask on success.
File type matching scans the context names list for entries with a set inode whose type bits equal the requested mode. Missing context or absence of a qualifying entry yields no match.

Directory tree matching yields no match for a null tree. Otherwise it scans fully populated reference chunks followed by the partially populated current chunk, reporting a match when any stored chunk entry matches the given tree.

Cross field identity comparison dispatches on the stored selector to cover process to object user and group relations as well as inter credential user to user and group to group relations with the field operator. Object forms succeed when the supplied name or any names list entry satisfies comparison. Unknown selectors warn and yield no match.
Mask membership first rejects values outside the thirty two bit range and word indexes outside bitmask capacity, then tests the corresponding bit in the rule mask.

Parent teardown acquires the filter mutex and then walks watches and their rules with safe iteration. Each rule removal is logged, executable marks are detached, the rule is unlinked from management lists and the RCU list with deferred reclamation, and the watch is removed. The mutex is released before destroying the parent filesystem notification mark.

The filesystem notification inode handler resolves the audit parent from the mark and verifies group ownership, ignoring mismatched groups with a one time warning. Creation and move in events update tracking with device and inode, deletion and move out events update with unset markers, and self deletion, unmount and self move trigger full parent teardown.

Watch subsystem initialization allocates a filesystem notification group bound to the audit handlers. Allocation failure clears the group reference and triggers the audit panic path while still reporting successful initialization.
The filesystem notification operations table statically binds the inode event handler and the mark release handler for the audit watch group.

Filtering maintains two parallel arrays of eight list heads each for live filtering and rule management views, with compile time enforcement of the count. A dedicated mutex serializes mutation of these lists.
An operator translation table maps internal comparator selectors for equality, inequality, bitmask, bit test and ordered comparisons to external audit operator codes.
The class registry is a fixed size array of pointers to thirty two bit word arrays, one entry per syscall class, initially null until registration installs a populated mask.
Initial priority bounds use half of the all ones unsigned sixty four bit value for the low bound and one less than that half for the high bound.
Filter arrays contain eight entries, tree reference chunks hold thirty one slots each, and syscall numbers are validated against bitmask word capacity scaled by thirty two.

Inode filtering holds RCU read side protection across the names list walk, rule lists are traversed with RCU list iteration, and task credentials are obtained through RCU dereference validated for the current task or creation path.

Watch parent teardown serializes watch and rule list mutation with the filter mutex. Rule entries unlinked from the RCU list are reclaimed asynchronously through an RCU callback that recovers the containing entry and releases it via the standard rule free path.
The RCU reclamation handler recovers the containing audit entry from the callback header and releases it through the standard rule free path.

Duplication and registration distinguish memory exhaustion from other failures. Partial duplication detaches any installed executable mark and frees the new entry before reporting failure. Invalid LSM policy is retained with a warning to allow later reload success. Registration rejects range violations and duplicate class installation without installing state.

Out of range syscall numbers, classes and mask words safely yield no match rather than accessing beyond storage. Missing syscall context, socket address or names entries yield no match for dependent selectors. Audit daemon tasks bypass inode filtering, unknown cross field selectors warn, and unexpected notification groups warn once and are ignored.
Logging in this compilation unit prefixes each message with the module name followed by a separator.
